summary.en-US: Per-page request firewall with geoip, geosite, domain/URL regex, and IP range rules

description.en-US:
GeoLock is a Firefox extension that gives you fine-grained control over sub-resource requests on a per-page basis.

For every request initiated by a webpage, GeoLock evaluates a configurable list of rules and decides whether to block or allow it. Rules can match on:

• geoip — country code from a v2fly-format database (resolved via DNS at runtime)
• geosite — domain category from a v2fly-format database
• domain — regular expression against the host
• url — regular expression against the full URL
• ip — CIDR (IPv4 or IPv6)
• logical combinators: AND, OR, NOT, with optional bidirectional matching

Rules support a website matcher (where the request was initiated) and a resource matcher (the request target), with separate evaluation for each side. A rule fires only when its conditions definitively match; rules abstain when the data needed to decide is missing, falling through to the next rule or the default action.

GeoIP/Geosite databases are not bundled. You configure HTTPS URLs to v2fly-format .dat files and GeoLock fetches and caches them on a schedule of your choice.

No telemetry. No data leaves your browser except DNS lookups and the data-source URLs you configure.

Source: https://github.com/mazzz1y/geolock

version.approval_notes:
Build: npm ci && npm run build. Plain ES modules, no bundler or minification. Tests: node tests/run.mjs (139 unit tests, all passing).

Permissions:
- webRequest + webRequestBlocking: required to inspect and cancel sub-resource requests as the rules engine matches them.
- webNavigation: required to associate sub-resource requests with the originating page (frame tracking).
- host_permissions <all_urls>: required because the firewall must see every outgoing request to apply rules; cannot be narrowed without losing core functionality.
- dns: used to resolve hostnames for geoip/ip matchers; lookups are local to the browser.
- storage, alarms: configuration persistence and scheduled geo-data updates.

No telemetry, no analytics, no remote code. data_collection_permissions is set to ["none"] in manifest.json. Geo databases are fetched from user-configured HTTPS URLs at runtime; no databases are bundled.

Android: gecko_android.strict_min_version is 142.0 in manifest.json (matches desktop floor). MV3 background scripts (event-page style) are used; no service workers.
